label: M-01
title: The pairing ratio is taken on trust from the minter's registered `decimals`; the dangerous direction fails OPEN and is permissionlessly exploitable
fingerprintNote: sha256(contract:function:rootCauseClass)[:16] - legacy form, empty entryPoint. Carried verbatim from sanitized.json; reproduces from fingerprintBasis.
sources: SA-010(semantic risk at the same lines)

classification.assetImpact: While armed, any antimatter holder mints ~2x phUSD while surrendering ~1e-10 of the stablecoin. The stable leg - the half that is supposed to be fully collateralised - becomes backed by dust. Unbounded in size (up to all outstanding antimatter) and unbounded in time (no revert, no event anomaly, no on-chain signal). Loss lands on phUSD holders as collateral dilution.
attackPath: 0. ARMING (owner, unknowing): an 18-decimal stablecoin is registered in PhusdStableMinter with decimals understated (e.g. 6). One mistyped argument.
1. Antimatter reads that value verbatim at :250 and never cross-checks IERC20Metadata(stable).decimals(), although it holds the token address and one staticcall would settle it.
2. scale becomes 1e12, so toStableAmount collapses the stablecoin pull by 1e12x. BOTH contracts make the identical error, so it cancels inside calculateMintAmount and nothing reverts.
3. Any holder calls annihilateFrom: 100 AM + 1e8 raw units of an 18-dp stablecoin -> 200e18 phUSD. The :230 residue check and the :233 non-zero receipt both pass.
4. Repeat permissionlessly until the misconfiguration is noticed by some out-of-band means.
classification.likelihood: Low to arm (a deliberate single owner argument that is normally correct), then HIGH and permissionless once armed, with no self-limiting mechanism and no signal that would prompt anyone to look.
classification.assumptions: A registered stablecoin's `decimals` is understated relative to its true ERC20 decimals. Antimatter emission is live enough that some holder has antimatter.
classification.externalRequirements: The owner misconfiguration at registration time (in PhusdStableMinter.registerStablecoin, a nested-submodule contract; filed against Antimatter because Antimatter acts on the value, doubles the blast radius with a second uncollateralised leg, and can defend itself in one line).

justification: FOOTGUN TEST (Law 3) - VALID, NOT SUPPRESSED. The misconfiguration is SURPRISING, not obvious, and the asymmetry is what proves it: the SAME mistake in the other direction (decimals overstated) is incidentally NOISY - the pull is 1e12x too large and safeTransferFrom typically reverts. That revert is NOT a guard: it is ERC20InsufficientBalance from the token's own transferFrom, so a sufficiently-funded caller is silently over-charged ~1e12x instead of reverting. The asymmetry still holds for ordinary balances and still supports the footgun ruling, but must not be written up as a fail-closed control. An owner who has seen, or reasonably expects, a loud revert from a wrong decimals argument has every reason to believe the parameter is self-checking. Instead the dangerous direction is silently absorbed at full phUSD issuance. A competent, non-malicious owner would be surprised; surprise => footgun => in scope. This explicitly OVERRIDES the faithfulness tier's Law-3 suppression of the same item as 'the minter owner's obvious single-step act' - it is not obvious, because it is silent. SEVERITY - MEDIUM, and the reason it is not High is stated plainly rather than hedged: the post-arming exploit IS permissionless, deterministic and unbounded, which is High-shaped, but the path is not free of external requirements - it needs a misconfiguration that does not exist in any observed deployment. C4 Medium is exactly 'value leak with a hypothetical attack path with stated assumptions, but external requirements'. It is not Low because the consequence is neither dust nor cosmetic: it is an unbounded permissionless free mint against the collateral base, PoC'd, with an intentional control (the exactness guard, machine-proven sound by Halmos) that provides no protection at all here because the guard is correct GIVEN a correct decimals - the proof is precisely why the registered value carries the whole risk. It is also not a 'weird ERC20' finding: the token is standard; the defect is unvalidated trust in a registered value.
recommendation: In toStableAmount cross-check the registered value: `if (decimals != IERC20Metadata(stable).decimals()) revert DecimalsMismatch(...)` (try/catch, revert if the token has no decimals()). This makes BOTH directions fail closed - note the overstated direction is not currently fail-closed either; it merely tends to trip ERC20InsufficientBalance in the token.

additionalContext.rootCause: Antimatter computes its entire economic premise from `decimals` read out of PhusdStableMinter.stablecoinConfigs, a value registerStablecoin accepts verbatim and never checks against IERC20Metadata(stablecoin).decimals(). Antimatter performs no independent check although it holds the token address and could do so in one staticcall.
additionalContext.asymmetry: decimals OVERSTATED (6-dp registered as 18): scale collapses to 1, the pull is 1e12x too large, and safeTransferFrom TYPICALLY reverts - but this is NOT a guard: the revert is ERC20InsufficientBalance raised by the token's own transferFrom, i.e. an accident of the caller's balance. A sufficiently-funded caller is SILENTLY OVER-CHARGED ~1e12x with no revert. Correctly described as incidentally noisy for ordinary balances, not as failing closed. decimals UNDERSTATED (18-dp registered as 6): scale becomes 1e12, the pull collapses by 1e12x, BOTH contracts make the same error so it cancels inside calculateMintAmount and nothing reverts - fails OPEN, silently, at full phUSD issuance.
additionalContext.impact: Any antimatter holder can permissionlessly receive 200 phUSD per 100 AM while surrendering 1e8 raw units (1e-10) of the stablecoin. The stable leg of phUSD - the leg that is supposed to be fully collateralised - becomes backed by dust, for as long as the misconfiguration stands and for as much antimatter as exists. No revert, no event anomaly, no on-chain signal; the :230 residue check and :233 non-zero receipt both pass.
additionalContext.footgunTest: Law 3 - an owner mis-typing one decimals argument would expect a revert or a proportionally wrong ratio, NOT a silent unbounded permissionless free-mint. Surprise => footgun => in scope.
additionalContext.rootCauseLocation: Registration-time validation gap is PhusdStableMinter.registerStablecoin (nested submodule, excluded at the findings layer). Filed against Antimatter because it reads and acts on the value, doubles the blast radius by minting a second uncollateralised leg on top, and can defend itself in one line. Flag for the minter's own audit.
